questions.disambiguation_rule: One of the eight planets recognised by the International Astronomical Union.
questions.disambiguation_detail: The IAU's 2006 resolution is the standard. Dwarf planets, moons, stars, and comets are separate categories and do not count, however large or familiar they are.

items.label: Mercury
items.source_1_note: IAU Resolution B5 footnote 1: the eight planets are Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.
items.source_2_note: IAU: the 2006 resolution means the Solar System officially consists of those eight planets.

items.label: Venus
items.source_1_note: IAU Resolution B5 footnote 1: named in the enumerated list of eight planets.
items.source_2_note: IAU: named in the official list of eight planets.

items.label: Mars
items.source_1_note: IAU Resolution B5 footnote 1: named in the enumerated list of eight planets.
items.source_2_note: IAU: named in the official list of eight planets.

items.label: Jupiter
items.source_1_note: IAU Resolution B5 footnote 1: named in the enumerated list of eight planets.
items.source_2_note: IAU: named in the official list of eight planets.

items.label: Neptune
items.source_1_note: IAU Resolution B5 footnote 1: named in the enumerated list of eight planets.
items.source_2_note: IAU: named in the official list of eight planets.

items.label: Pluto
items.source_1_note: IAU Resolution B6: Pluto is a dwarf planet and prototype of a new category of Trans-Neptunian Objects.
items.source_2_note: Library of Congress: IAU downgraded Pluto to dwarf planet in August 2006, leaving eight planets.

items.label: Ceres
items.source_1_note: IAU names Ceres among the recognised dwarf planets alongside Pluto, Haumea, Makemake and Eris.

items.label: The Moon
items.source_1_note: Not among the eight planets enumerated in footnote 1. The resolution treats satellites as a distinct category.

items.label: The Sun
items.source_1_note: The definition requires a planet to orbit the Sun, which excludes the Sun itself. Not among the eight.

items.label: Halley's Comet
items.source_1_note: Footnote 3 places comets among Small Solar-System Bodies, a category distinct from planets.

questions.disambiguation_rule: Develops from the flower's ovary and contains seeds.
questions.disambiguation_detail: Culinary category is irrelevant. A vegetable in the kitchen can be a fruit in botany. Judged on the part of the plant eaten as that food, not on other parts the same plant produces.

items.label: Tomato
items.source_1_note: Names tomatoes among foods technically fruits under the ripened-ovary definition.
items.source_2_note: Lists tomatoes as fruits and further as true berries.

items.label: Cucumber
items.source_1_note: Names cucumbers among foods technically fruits.
items.source_2_note: Includes cucumbers among botanical berries, a class of fruit.

items.label: Avocado
items.source_1_note: Names avocados among foods technically fruits.
items.source_2_note: States avocados are botanically berries.

items.label: Pumpkin
items.source_1_note: Lists pumpkin among fruits alongside squash, cucumber and tomato.
items.source_2_note: Names pumpkins among botanical fruits under the mature-ovary definition.

items.label: Olive
items.source_1_note: Defines the drupe or stone fruit as a fruit type with fleshy exocarp and mesocarp around a hardened endocarp enclosing a seed.
items.source_2_note: Names olives explicitly among foods qualifying as botanical fruits.

items.label: Rhubarb
items.source_1_note: States rhubarb is not a fruit but the petiole of a poisonous leaf.

items.label: Broccoli
items.source_1_note: Brooklyn Botanic Garden: broccoli florets are unopened flower buds.

items.label: Potato
items.source_1_note: Classifies potatoes among edible tubers, or underground stems.

items.label: Celery
items.source_1_note: Classifies celery among leaf and leafstalk vegetables.

items.label: Lettuce
items.source_1_note: Classifies lettuce among leaf and leafstalk vegetables.

questions.category_title: Chemical elements named after a place
questions.disambiguation_rule: Named after a geographic place on Earth.
questions.disambiguation_detail: Named after a person, a mythological figure, a celestial body, or a physical property does not count. Latinised and historical place names count.

items.label: Americium
items.source_1_note: Listed; named after the United States of America.
items.source_2_note: Names americium after America among elements named for countries.

items.label: Polonium
items.source_1_note: Listed; named after Poland.
items.source_2_note: Takes its name from Polonia, the Latin name for Poland.

items.label: Copper
items.source_1_note: Listed under Cyprus.
items.source_2_note: Latin cuprum descends from Kyprios, the Greek name for Cyprus. Some sources hedge with probably.

items.label: Curium
items.source_1_note: Absent from the place-named list. Honours Marie and Pierre Curie.

items.label: Einsteinium
items.source_1_note: Absent from the place-named list. Honours Albert Einstein.

items.label: Titanium
items.source_1_note: Absent from the place-named list. Named after the Titans, not the moon Titan.

items.label: Mercury
items.source_1_note: Absent from the place-named list. Named after the god Mercury, not the planet.

items.label: Helium
items.source_1_note: Absent from the place-named list. Named for the Sun, a celestial body.

items.label: Selenium
items.source_1_note: Absent from the place-named list. Named for the Moon, a celestial body.

items.label: Uranium
items.source_1_note: Absent from the place-named list. Named for the planet Uranus, a celestial body.

questions.category_title: Sports that have been medal events at a Summer Olympics
questions.disambiguation_rule: Has been a medal event at a Summer Olympic Games through 2024.
questions.disambiguation_detail: Discontinued sports still count. Demonstration sports do not count. Winter Games do not count. Sports scheduled for future Games but not yet held do not count.

items.label: Race walking
items.source_1_note: Race walking is a continuing athletics event on the Summer Olympic programme.
items.source_2_note: Listed among current Olympic athletics events.

items.label: Trampoline
items.source_1_note: Trampoline gymnastics is a current Olympic discipline, medal event since 2000.
items.source_2_note: Referenced among Olympic gymnastics disciplines.

items.label: Solo synchronised swimming
items.source_1_note: Medal event from the 1984 Los Angeles Games through 1992, replaced by the team event in 1996.
items.source_2_note: Confirms the event ran at Los Angeles, Seoul and Barcelona before becoming a team event.

items.label: Tug of war
items.source_1_note: Olympic event from 1900 to 1920 as part of the track and field programme, discontinued after Antwerp 1920.
items.source_2_note: Sports historian David Goldblatt confirms it was an Olympic sport from 1900 to 1920.

items.label: Croquet
items.source_1_note: Played at the 1900 Paris Games; first Olympic sport in which women competed. France won gold in individual and doubles.
items.source_2_note: Confirms croquet's single appearance at the 1900 Paris Games including the first women competitors.

items.label: Darts
items.source_1_note: Not among Olympic sports past or present.

items.label: Chess
items.source_1_note: IOC-recognised but never a medal event at a Summer Olympics.

items.label: Netball
items.source_1_note: IOC-recognised but never a medal event at a Summer Olympics.

items.label: Snooker
items.source_1_note: Never a medal event at a Summer Olympics.

items.label: Squash
items.source_1_note: Not yet a medal event. Scheduled to debut at Los Angeles 2028, which the through-2024 rule excludes.

questions.category_title: Marques that began producing automobiles before 1920
questions.disambiguation_rule: The company sold its first production automobile before 1 January 1920.
questions.disambiguation_detail: Company founding date does not count if the company made something else first. Trademark registration does not count. Prototypes and one-off vehicles do not count. What matters is the first automobile offered for sale.

items.label: Ford
items.source_1_note: Names the 1903 Ford Model A as the Model B's predecessor; Ford Motor Company incorporated June 1903.
items.source_2_note: Ford Motor Company formed June 1903; first Model A sold to Chicago dentist Ernest Pfennig that year.

items.label: Cadillac
items.source_1_note: First Cadillac automobiles were the 1903 model, built in the last quarter of 1902.
items.source_2_note: Cadillac Automobile Company established 22 August 1902; first automobile completed October 1902.

items.label: Buick
items.source_1_note: Model B was Buick's first model as an independent company, introduced 13 August 1904.
items.source_2_note: First production Buick was the 1904 Model B; first sale August 1904, 37 built that year.

items.label: Peugeot
items.source_1_note: Type 2, first petrol-powered Peugeot, produced 1890 to 1891 at Valentigney.
items.source_2_note: Peugeot's own history: three Type 2 units produced March to July 1890.

items.label: Renault
items.source_1_note: Voiturette was Renault's first produced automobile, first sold 24 December 1898 with twelve more orders that night.
items.source_2_note: Renault's own museum: Type A ready by Christmas 1898; twelve friends ordered one after the Rue Lepic climb.

items.label: Volvo
items.source_1_note: First car, the Volvo OV 4, rolled off the line in 1927. Trademark registered 1915 for ball bearings, never used for cars.
items.source_2_note: Volvo Group's own history: first series-manufactured Volvo car, the OV4, in 1927.

items.label: Ferrari
items.source_1_note: 125 S was the first vehicle to bear the Ferrari name, debut 11 May 1947. Preceded by the 1940 Auto Avio Costruzioni 815, which did not carry the name.

items.label: Toyota
items.source_1_note: Toyoda Spinning and Weaving founded 1918; first car the Model AA in 1936; Toyota Motor Company established 1937.

items.label: Subaru
items.source_1_note: Subaru 1500, code name P-1, was the first car built by Fuji Heavy Industries. Produced 1954, twenty units.

items.label: Kia
items.source_1_note: Founded 1944 as Kyungsung Precision Industry. Motorcycles from 1957, trucks from 1962. First car the Brisa in 1974.

questions.category_title: Correct airport code and city pairings
questions.disambiguation_rule: The three-letter IATA code assigned to an airport serving the named city.
questions.disambiguation_detail: Judged on the code as officially assigned, not on how well the letters seem to fit the city. Cities with several airports have several codes; any correctly assigned one counts.

items.label: CDG — Paris
items.source_1_note: IATA CDG, primary international airport serving Paris.
items.source_2_note: Lists Paris (PAR) with Charles de Gaulle (CDG) among its airports.

items.label: NRT — Tokyo
items.source_1_note: IATA's own city code list gives NRT as Narita Intl serving Tokyo.
items.source_2_note: NRT listed as Tokyo Narita.

items.label: YYZ — Toronto
items.source_1_note: IATA YYZ, serving the Greater Toronto Area.
items.source_2_note: Cites YYZ for Toronto among Canada's weather-station-derived codes.

items.label: GRU — São Paulo
items.source_1_note: IATA GRU, primary international airport serving São Paulo.
items.source_2_note: GRU listed for São Paulo.

items.label: SVO — Moscow
items.source_1_note: Lists Moscow (MOW) with Sheremetyevo (SVO) among its airports.
items.source_2_note: IATA's own list gives SVO Sheremetyevo under Moscow.

items.label: LAX — Lagos
items.source_1_note: PENDING. LAX is Los Angeles International. Lagos is LOS.

items.label: DUB — Dubai
items.source_1_note: DUB is Dublin. Dubai is DXB.

items.label: PEK — Perth
items.source_1_note: PENDING. PEK is Beijing Capital. Perth is PER.

items.label: BER — Bern
items.source_1_note: Lists Berlin's self-named code as BER. Bern is BRN.

items.label: BOM — Boston
items.source_1_note: PENDING. BOM is Mumbai. Boston is BOS.
